claim.quote: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP liquid argon time projection chamber performance from a beam test at the CERN Neutrino Platform

date.note: First public posting (arXiv v1, 13 July 2020), before the JINST 15 (2020) P12004 publication; the display date is the earliest public date.

name: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP single-phase LArTPC performance in a beam test
notes: date_kind is preprint (arXiv v1, 13 July 2020); the paper was published as JINST 15 (2020) P12004.
This is a construction/technology milestone, not a physics discovery, evidence claim or measurement; this atlas holds no DUNE physics result.

significance.note: A technology milestone, not a physics measurement; no single headline number is quoted.

summary.plain: ProtoDUNE-SP is a prototype of DUNE's first far-detector module, built with full-size components and tested in a particle beam at CERN. The paper reports measured values that meet or exceed the DUNE far-detector specifications, and says its successful operation demonstrates the effectiveness of the single-phase far-detector design.
summary.technical: ProtoDUNE-SP (NP04), a single-phase LArTPC with an active volume of 7.2 × 6.0 × 6.9 m³ at the CERN Neutrino Platform, exposed to a charged-particle beam of 0.3-7 GeV/c; the paper reports first performance results (noise and gain, dE/dx calibration, drift electron lifetime, photon-detector noise, sensitivity and time resolution): the measured values meet or exceed the DUNE far-detector specifications, in several cases by large margins.

title: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP liquid argon time projection chamber performance from a beam test at the CERN Neutrino Platform
why_it_matters: The abstract states that the measured values meet or exceed the specifications for the DUNE far detector, and that ProtoDUNE-SP's successful operation starting in 2018 and its large samples of high-quality data demonstrate the effectiveness of the single-phase far detector design.
